stories.title: China's 'Justice Mission 2025' drills rehearse a blockade of Taiwan
stories.summary: For two days (Dec 29–30) the PLA ran joint live-fire drills around Taiwan, which Beijing called a 'stern warning' to separatist and 'external interference' forces. ISW assessed that the exercise rehearsed a blockade and counter-intervention, with coast guard ships enforcing it. Beijing tied the drills to what could be the largest-ever US arms sale to Taiwan and to Japanese PM Takaichi's Taiwan remarks. Taiwan said more than 100,000 air travellers were affected.

causes.why: The 2022 encirclement drills set the template that each new exercise extends

analysis.text: Beijing is normalising blockade rehearsals so that a real quarantine would look like routine, and it is pairing military pressure on Taipei with coercion of Tokyo.

stories.unplaced: Drills ran in several zones around Taiwan; there is no single site.

stories.title: US strikes Venezuela and captures Maduro
stories.summary: The United States carried out a 'large-scale strike' on Venezuela early on Jan 3. Nicolás Maduro and his wife were captured and flown to New York to face narco-terrorism charges. Trump said the US would 'run' the country at least temporarily, and said Vice President and oil minister Delcy Rodríguez was willing to work with Washington as acting president.

causes.why: Washington's 2022 energy bargaining failed to move Maduro; in 2026 it switched from bargaining to force

analysis.text: The stated case is narcotics; the real aims look like control of Venezuelan oil and pushing China, Russia and Iran out of the hemisphere. It also made later US threats against Mexico and Cuba credible.

stories.title: Caracas agrees to ship oil to the US under Washington's control
stories.summary: Trump said Venezuela would export up to $2 billion of crude (30–50 million barrels) to the United States, diverting supply from China. Under the deal, the US would market the oil and put the proceeds in US-controlled accounts. Trading houses Trafigura and Vitol began marketing it, and Indian refiners said in late January that they were being offered only small volumes.

causes.why: The raid gave Washington control of the acting government's oil decisions

stories.unplaced: An agreement announced from Washington; no physical site.

stories.title: Iran crushes nationwide protests; thousands killed
stories.summary: Protests that began in late December 2025 over economic hardship turned against the regime and were suppressed under a nationwide internet and phone blackout. The activist group HRANA confirmed 6,221 deaths by Jan 27 and 7,005 by Feb 12, with thousands more under investigation. Trump threatened US strikes if Iran kept killing protesters and sent naval forces to the region.

causes.why: Same pattern: a protest wave met by mass force, deepening the regime's legitimacy gap

analysis.text: The killings gave Washington and Israel a political case and a reading that the regime was brittle, which fed the decision to strike in February.

stories.unplaced: Nationwide protests and crackdown; there is no single site.

stories.title: Yemen's southern separatists announce disbanding as a Saudi–UAE rift opens
stories.summary: After the UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council pushed into Hadramaut and al-Mahra in December, a Saudi-backed counteroffensive retook the areas. On Jan 9, STC members in Riyadh announced the council's dissolution. STC leaders called the decision coerced and void, and thousands rallied in Aden on Jan 10 in support of the group.

causes.why: The 2022 council bundled Saudi- and UAE-backed factions; that bargain broke in 2026

analysis.text: Riyadh took sole control of the anti-Houthi camp and sidelined Abu Dhabi's proxy. The same Saudi–UAE split resurfaced in April when the UAE quit OPEC.

stories.title: Congo's army returns to Uvira after M23 withdraws under US pressure
stories.summary: Congolese troops returned to the strategic eastern town of Uvira, near the Burundi border, after M23 rebels withdrew. The pullout followed US pressure linked to the Washington peace accords between Congo and Rwanda.

causes.why: M23's 2022 resurgence began the expansion that reached Uvira

stories.title: Trump drops Greenland tariff threat after European troops deploy
stories.summary: Trump had threatened 10% tariffs, rising to 25% in June, on eight European countries that joined Denmark's Operation Arctic Endurance in Greenland. At Davos on Jan 21 he dropped the tariffs, said he would not use force, and announced a 'framework' on Arctic security after talks with NATO's Mark Rutte. Denmark and Greenland rejected any transfer of sovereignty.

analysis.text: Allies learned that collective pushback works, and also that Washington will use tariffs against NATO members. Both lessons pushed Europe to hedge, including with the India trade deal days later.

stories.title: India and the EU conclude the 'mother of all trade deals'
stories.summary: India and the European Union announced the conclusion of a free trade agreement after nearly two decades of talks, cutting tariffs on a broad range of goods and services. The deal still needs legal vetting and approval in Brussels and New Delhi before it takes effect.

causes.why: US tariff threats against allies pushed both sides to lock in other markets

stories.unplaced: Negotiated deal with no single signing site in the sources.

stories.title: Clashes erupt in Tigray; Ethiopian Airlines halts flights
stories.summary: Fighting broke out between Ethiopian federal troops and Tigrayan forces in western Tigray. Ethiopian Airlines cancelled flights to the region as fears grew of a return to war.
stories.unplaced: Western Tigray fighting; the sources name no town we can pin.

stories.title: Sudan's army breaks the RSF sieges of Dilling and Kadugli
stories.summary: The Sudanese army said it broke the Rapid Support Forces' nearly two-year siege of Dilling in late January, then the siege of famine-stricken Kadugli, the capital of South Kordofan, on Feb 3. The RSF had taken the army base at Babanusa in West Kordofan in December 2025.

causes.why: The 2021 coup left the army and RSF sharing power, the split that became today's war

analysis.text: Kordofan has become the war's centre of gravity: whoever holds it controls the road between Darfur and the Nile heartland.

stories.title: New START expires; no limits remain on US and Russian nuclear forces
stories.summary: The last US–Russia strategic arms treaty expired on Feb 5. Moscow said it would keep to the old limits only if Washington did, and the US said it wanted a broader deal that includes China. US officials met Russian and Chinese delegations later in February, but China resisted formal three-way talks.
stories.unplaced: A treaty lapse; no physical site.

stories.title: US cuts India tariffs to 18% after a pledge to curb Russian oil
stories.summary: Washington dropped its separate 25% punitive tariff on India and cut the overall rate from 50% to 18% under an interim trade framework, after India pledged to cut purchases of Russian oil. Within a month the Iran war hit supplies and Indian refiners were again buying prompt Russian cargoes under a US waiver.

causes.why: India's EU deal strengthened its hand with Washington

stories.unplaced: A trade framework with no event site.

stories.title: Takaichi wins a landslide despite Chinese coercion over Taiwan
stories.summary: Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi won a supermajority in the Feb 8 lower-house election. Beijing had retaliated for her November 2025 remark that a Taiwan contingency could draw a Japanese military response, with travel warnings, flight cuts, a seafood import ban and curbs on dual-use exports including rare earths. CSIS judged the campaign failed to weaken her.

causes.why: Beijing tied its pressure on Japan to Takaichi's Taiwan remarks

stories.unplaced: A national election; no single site.

stories.title: Supreme Court strikes down Trump's IEEPA tariffs; a 10% global tariff replaces them
stories.summary: In Learning Resources v. Trump the Supreme Court held that the emergency-powers law IEEPA does not let the president impose tariffs, voiding the 'reciprocal' and drug-trafficking tariffs. Trump ordered a temporary 10% global tariff for 150 days under Section 122 from Feb 24 and new trade probes under other laws.

analysis.text: Losing IEEPA took away the fastest tariff weapon, which made trade deals and sector-specific tariffs Washington's main levers for the rest of the year.

stories.unplaced: A court ruling and executive orders; no event site.

stories.title: Mexican forces kill CJNG boss 'El Mencho' in a US-backed raid
stories.summary: Mexican special forces killed Nemesio 'El Mencho' Oseguera, leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, in Tapalpa, Jalisco. US intelligence, including a new Pentagon-led task force, helped find him. The cartel answered with roadblocks and arson across Mexico. President Sheinbaum said US forces shared intelligence but did not take part.

causes.why: The Caracas raid made the threat of unilateral US action against cartels credible

analysis.text: Mexico delivered a major scalp on its own terms to head off unilateral US strikes on its soil.

stories.title: Pakistan declares 'open war' on Taliban-ruled Afghanistan
stories.summary: After days of cross-border fighting, Pakistan's defence minister said the country was in 'open war' with Afghanistan, and Pakistani jets struck targets in Kabul, Kandahar and other provinces. The Taliban said it was open to talks.

causes.why: Al-Qaeda's leader sheltering in Kabul showed the Taliban hosting militants, the core of Pakistan's complaint

analysis.text: Islamabad blames the Taliban for sheltering the Pakistani Taliban (TTP). Its former proxy has become an enemy.

stories.title: US and Israel strike Iran and kill Khamenei; Iran hits back and bars Hormuz
stories.summary: The US and Israel launched strikes on Iranian military and leadership targets (the US called it Operation Epic Fury), and Iranian state media confirmed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed. Iran fired missiles and drones at Israel and US bases in the Gulf, and ships were told by VHF that Hormuz transit was 'banned'.

causes.why: The crackdown framed the regime as brittle and gave Washington a political case
With no nuclear deal since 2022, force became the default tool

analysis.text: The aim looks like regime decapitation more than counter-proliferation. Iran's answer, closing Hormuz, turned a regional war into a global energy shock.

stories.title: Hezbollah joins the war; Israel invades southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired rockets and drones at Israel on Mar 2 in retaliation for Khamenei's killing. Israel resumed heavy strikes and sent ground troops into southern Lebanon. By Mar 24 its defence minister said the army would occupy a swathe of the south.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Timeline of the Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2 March 2026 – present)

causes.why: Hezbollah entered to avenge Khamenei

stories.unplaced: Fighting across southern Lebanon and northern Israel; no single site.

stories.title: Iran names Mojtaba Khamenei supreme leader
stories.summary: Iran's Assembly of Experts chose Mojtaba Khamenei, a hardliner and son of the slain leader, as the Islamic Republic's third supreme leader. Oil prices rose on the news.

causes.why: Succession forced by Khamenei's killing

analysis.text: Decapitation produced continuity, not collapse: a younger hardliner tied to the IRGC now leads.

stories.unplaced: The Assembly's meeting place was not disclosed.

stories.title: IEA orders a record 400-million-barrel emergency stock release
stories.summary: IEA members agreed to release a record 400 million barrels of emergency oil stocks as the Iran war cut Hormuz flows. The US pledged 172.2 million barrels and Japan about 80 million. The IEA said the world faced the largest oil supply disruption on record.

causes.why: Hormuz closure
2022 reserve releases set the playbook

stories.unplaced: A policy decision; no physical site.

stories.title: US bombs military sites on Kharg Island, Iran's oil export hub
stories.summary: US aircraft struck missile and mine storage sites on Kharg Island, which handles about 90% of Iran's crude exports. Officials said oil infrastructure was left intact on purpose, and Trump warned it could be hit if Iran kept interfering with Hormuz shipping.

causes.why: Escalation to pressure Iran over Hormuz

analysis.text: Washington held Iran's oil lifeline hostage instead of destroying it, a bargaining chip for reopening Hormuz.

stories.title: Cuba confirms talks with Washington as the US oil blockade bites
stories.summary: Cuban leader Miguel Díaz-Canel confirmed talks with the Trump administration as a US oil blockade, which followed the cut-off of Venezuelan supply, deepened shortages and blackouts.

causes.why: Loss of Venezuelan oil left Cuba exposed to a US blockade

stories.title: Pakistani airstrike on a Kabul hospital kills hundreds
stories.summary: Pakistani airstrikes hit a hospital in Kabul. Wikipedia's account of the strike, citing news reports, puts the dead at more than 400.

causes.why: Escalating air campaign

stories.title: Big Tech turns to record borrowing to fund AI data centers
stories.summary: Analysts raised their forecasts for hyperscaler debt after an Amazon bond sale. UBS later estimated hyperscalers had issued about $274 billion of investment-grade debt in 2026, plus about $169 billion of data-center-specific issuance, as AI capex outran cash flow.

causes.why: AI compute became a strategic commodity worth borrowing for

analysis.text: Debt-funded AI build-out ties tech valuations to long-term interest rates, the link that bit in October.

stories.title: US, Congo and Rwanda recommit to the Washington Accords
stories.summary: The US, Congo and Rwanda issued a joint statement on advancing the Washington Accords, which require Rwanda to withdraw its forces and Congo to neutralise the FDLR militia. A separate Doha track covers talks between Kinshasa and AFC/M23.

causes.why: Uvira pullout was the first test of the accords

analysis.text: Washington's interest is minerals access as much as peace; the accords give US firms a path into eastern Congo's supply chain.

stories.title: China sanctions a close Takaichi aide over Taiwan visits
stories.summary: China sanctioned Japanese lawmaker Keiji Furuya, head of a cross-party Japan–Taiwan group and a close aide to PM Takaichi, for 'collusion' with Taiwan independence forces. Tokyo called it 'absolutely unacceptable'.

causes.why: Beijing kept up pressure after the election
